transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Session begins. Each player has Ysolde 3 FP, Aldous 3 FP, Morwen 3 FP, Mire 3 FP. Face-up: Rising Floodwaters [H-03], Hive-Touched Pack [T-01].

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Rain hammers the reed roofs of Hollowmoot as the four of you shove off from the last dry dock, laden with what supplies you could beg or buy. Ahead, the causeway is already a memory — the only way south is through Gullet Ford, waist-deep and churning brown, its reed banks thick enough to hide anything. Somewhere out in that grey static of rain you can hear it: a wet, rhythmic slapping, like spears striking water in unison, moving along the treeline in a pattern that isn't quite natural. The river itself seems to be climbing even as you watch, swallowing the sandbar you meant to rest on. Whatever waits in the reeds, you'll have to cross before the ford drowns entirely.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: There—see where the current shifts? That's where the deep channel runs. We follow it, we can make it across before the water rises any higher.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde leans over the side of the barge, reading the churning brown water with the intimate knowledge of one born to the reeds. Her eyes track the patterns of foam and ripple, the subtle variations in depth and color that mark where the ford runs deep. Something hunts in the reeds, but she has swum these channels her whole life—exile hasn't taken that from her.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: They're pinned to the eastern bank—the rising water is driving them there, keeping them bunched together. That's where they'll stay until the ford drowns completely.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous stands very still as the rain hammers against his skin, his fingers tracing patterns in the air. He closes his eyes and listens—not to the thunder, but to the wet slapping sound in the distance, the rhythm of it becoming clear. He reads the omens written in how the water moves, how the current shifts with their passage, feeling the pack's intent through the surge and the reed-banks.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: I know what you are! I've sent plenty of your kind back to whatever choir calls to you—show yourselves or get out of our way!

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen stands in the bow, reading the wet rhythm in the reeds. That coordinated slapping—it's not feral thrashing, it's a hunt. She's heard this song before, broken it before. Her voice cuts across the ford with the weight of the Order behind it, an exorcist's authority that demands acknowledgment.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Hold steady. I can hear them moving—let me see where they are before we're caught mid-ford.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire rises slowly in the boat, every sense razor-sharp from years of watch drills in worse weather. She scans the grey static of reeds, tracking that wet rhythmic slapping, triangulating the sounds to pinpoint where the creatures are stalking along the banks before they realize how exposed we are crossing the ford.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — create advantage with Notice: dice + - - +, invoking Reads river currents like kin [YS-01] → Great (+4) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — create advantage with Notice: dice - + - + → Great (+4) vs Poor (-1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — create advantage with Lore: dice 0 - + + → Great (+4) vs Good (+3): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — create advantage with Notice: dice - 0 + 0 → Good (+3) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Between the four of you, the ford gives up every secret it had. Ysolde reads the deep channel true — the safe line runs clean from the sandbar to the far bank, and the barge answers her calls without a single scrape of mud. Aldous goes still and reads the pack's whole hunting pattern in the rhythm of the rain and the water's surge — not just where they are, but where the rising flood is herding them, penned tight against the eastern bank with no room to flank. Morwen's voice cracks out over the ford like a bell, and for a heartbeat the wet slapping in the reeds actually falters — they know her, or know what she's sent back to the swarm-song before. Mire's watch-trained eyes finish the picture, pinning the pack's exact position through the grey static of rain. By the time the barge noses into open water, you know the safe channel, the pack's pattern, their location, and that they're rattled by Morwen's challenge — everything you need to run this crossing clean, before the flood finishes swallowing the ford behind you.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: The channel holds. Keep your eyes sharp—they're caged now, and caged things bite at anything that moves.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde keeps one hand steady on the barge's tiller, guiding it deeper into the open water of the channel she read. Her eyes stay locked on the eastern bank where the pack writhes and churns, trapped between the rising flood and the trees—no escape route left. She's waiting to see if they'll do something desperate, if fear will override their hive-maddened hunting sense.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The water has them. We cross while they're pinned.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous stands motionless as the barge slides through the safe channel, his eyes never leaving the pack thrashing against the eastern bank. His fingers continue their rain-tracing patterns, reading the omens written in the flood's remorseless rise—watching to ensure his companions escape before the ford drowns entirely, using the water itself as a shield between them and the trapped hunters.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Come on then! I've sent your kind screaming back to whatever choir calls you—show yourselves and face an exorcist!

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen stands unshaking in the bow of the barge, blazing with the certainty of one who walked through the first outbreak untouched. She reaches toward the eastern bank where the pack crouches trapped by rising water, pressing her will forward like a blade. The words she speaks are old—rites of binding and breaking, each one a strike aimed at the heart of their hunger. She knows their pattern now, knows exactly where they crouch and how the flood has them pinned.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Follow Ysolde's line—she reads this water like I read a patrol route. Aldous, keep your ear on that pack; if they shift, we shift. Stay sharp, all of you—they're pinned for now, but only while we're crossing.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire keeps low in the boat's center, spear held ready but not raised, eyes tracking the eastern bank in the grey rain. She settles into the watch-captain's rhythm she never quite shed—the calm focus before things go hard. She positions herself between the crew and the reed-line, a barrier if the pack makes a play across the ford.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — attack with Will: dice - - - -, invoking Untouched by the swarm-song [MO-01], Raised in the Order's care [MO-01] → Great (+4) vs Good (+3): SUCCESS (Hive-Touched Pack (unseen, stalking) stress 1)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Morwen's binding-rite cracks across the water like a struck bell, and for the first time the wet slapping rhythm in the reeds breaks apart entirely — something in the pack flinches, stumbles, goes silent for three full heartbeats before the frenzy resumes, thinner now, less coordinated. The barge rides Ysolde's deep channel clean across the ford, Aldous calling the water's surge a breath before it happens, Mire's spear never leaving her hands but never needing to rise either. By the time the far bank's mud comes up under the hull, the eastern reeds are just noise behind you — the pack still caged there, still hunting, but the ford itself is between you now, and rising fast. You've crossed. Gullet Ford is already narrowing to a churning brown scar behind the barge, and whatever the pack does next, it does it on the wrong side of the water.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The barge grounds on a low hummock of reed and half-drowned stone on the ford's far side, and for a moment there's nothing but rain and the ragged sound of your own breathing. Behind you the pack's cries have faded into the grey — thinned, scattered, not gone. Ahead, the land rises just enough to promise something dry: a broken roofline, maybe, or the old stone track the Order is said to keep clear of the mire. Every hour you spend scouting is an hour the flood climbs behind you, and Gullet Ford won't stay a road home much longer. You have to choose a direction and commit to it before the light goes.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: There—that ridge holds high ground. The water won't catch us if we follow the stone inland. We have maybe four hours before the ford closes for good.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde moves to the barge's edge, rain streaming down her face. She studies the slope of the land ahead, reading how water pools in the hollows, how the ancient stone track rises just enough to escape the flood's grip. Her fingers trace the ridge line—she's done this a hundred times in a hundred marshes. This is the Reed-Kin's gift, whatever they tried to beat out of her.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The flood speaks clear—the stone track ahead runs high and dry. We push forward now, before darkness makes us blind.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous stands still in the downpour, face tilted to read the rain's patterns against the landscape. His gaze follows the water's surge across the drenched ground, the way stone rises just beyond the reeds. He points toward the dark line of the old track, reading the flood's rise with the certainty of someone who has learned to speak its language.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: The pack is scattered and maddened. We move now—hard and fast—before they remember how to hunt together. That high ground ahead could give us shelter or a defensible position. Show me it's solid.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen strides toward the prow, rain streaming down her face. She shields her eyes and sweeps her gaze across the elevated ground ahead—reading the broken roofline, tracing the old stone track, searching for threats or solid footing. Her jaw is set. No hesitation.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Give me a moment. I'm reading the land ahead before we commit.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire stands firm in the bow of the barge, rain streaming down her scarred face. She studies the landscape ahead with the careful, systematic eye of someone who spent years reading terrain from a guard post—tracing where the water meets the reed, looking for high ground and the true path forward. Her hand rests on her weapon out of habit.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — create advantage with Notice: dice + - + 0 → Good (+3) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — overcome with Notice: dice - + - -, invoking Reads omens in the rainfall [AL-01] → Great (+4) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — overcome with Notice: dice - - - -, invoking Knows the safest reed-paths [MO-02] → Mediocre (+0) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS MAJOR COST

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — overcome with Notice: dice - 0 0 + → Good (+3) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: The Order's stones. I trained there as a child. We move now, hard and fast.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire accepts the compel on 'Raised in the Temple Orphanage'.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The land answers everyone at once. Ysolde's read of the ridge holds true — water pools away from the stone, and the track rises clean and dry ahead. Aldous reads the flood's own rhythm in the rain and confirms it: they have their hours, the ford will close, but not yet. Morwen pushes her sight hardest of all, straining to map every hollow and shadow of the rise for threats — and gets her answer, but it costs her; the effort leaves her gasping, soaked through to the bone and shaking, a price paid in her own strength that she'll carry into whatever comes next. And Mire doesn't just see the stone track, she recognizes it — the worn steps, the drainage cut into the old flags, the watch-marks carved by Order novices generations back. 'The Order's stones. I trained there as a child.' The memory pulls at her, sharp and unbidden, of drills in the rain and a discipline that was the only family she ever had. She accepts it, lets it steady her hands rather than shake them, and pushes the party forward, hard and fast, up out of the reeds and onto dry stone at last. Behind you, Gullet Ford disappears into grey static; ahead, the old Order track climbs toward whatever waits at the top of the rise — and the four of you have left the causeway and the ford both behind for good.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: At the grave of a child lost to the swarm-song during the First Outbreak - I refused to let the Wardens burn even her body, and I spoke my vow aloud before all the mourners. Her aunt was there, holding what was left of her daughter's hand. Cartel picked that woman up for debt five years later and squeezed her for every secret she knew about the girl who stood against the torches.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: I'll go now - my vow won't let me refuse, and you know it. But if that house isn't actually burning, or if this is just a way to split us at the ford, understand what you've started. Name the location and I'm moving.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen accepts the compel on 'Vow Against the Burning'.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Beat: A gaunt scavenger who has been squatting inside the sunken cart wreck at Gullet Ford — watching every crossing for weeks — steps out into the rain. He's no drifter; he's a Cartel spotter, and he's been waiting for you specifically. turns on the party, because Word travels fast on the water: Morwen's open vow against the Wardens' torches has reached Cartel ears, and they've decided a healer who defies the men who burn houses is worth owning rather than losing to the Order or the Wardens..

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The scavenger doesn't run. He rises slow from behind the rusted ribs of the wreck, rain sheeting off a hood he never bothers to lower, and there's a wrongness to how still he stands after weeks alone with the hive-touched screaming in the reeds. "Morwen of the graveside vow," he says, like he's tasting the name. "The one who wouldn't let them burn a dead girl." Behind him, low whistles answer from the reed banks — more than one man, all along the wreck line, closing the only dry path off the ford before anyone's even drawn a blade. He's not here to talk toll. He's here to collect.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Hold, brother. I'm Ysolde, and I carry the Cartel's trust. Before this goes bitter, let's talk about what the Cartel actually wants from the healer and whether taking her bleeding into the reeds is how you get it done.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps forward from the barge party, water streaming from her cook's coat. Her hands are open and empty at her sides—neither weapon nor surrender. She keeps her voice steady and meets the Spotter's eyes with the quiet certainty of someone used to command in tight spaces.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The rain reads you, spotter. I've made a vow to cross every soul on these waters—and Morwen is under that vow now. Step back.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous steps forward sharply, placing himself directly between Morwen and the scavenger. His eyes scan the reed banks with preternatural accuracy, tracking movement as if the rain itself is whispering the positions of every armed man. He touches the iron charms at his neck—old river-tokens, talismans for those who've drowned and need safe passage across the flood.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: You thought my vow made me something you could own. You're about to learn how wrong that was.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps forward through the rain, drawing on the binding-rite power that still thrums through her bones. She channels the unyielding force of her vow against the spotter, meeting his rain-slicked gaze with spiritual presence he cannot match.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: The Cartel knows me. Wick Lane knows me. The debt is mine to pay, not hers — and you're going to take it from me first.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire steps through the rain to stand between Morwen and the scavenger, boots finding solid ground. Her hand rests on her sword hilt, weight forward, eyes steady on the man in the hood. She's not fast enough to stop them calling to the reeds, but fast enough to make sure they all bleed if they try to move past her.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — attack with Will: dice + 0 0 + → Fantastic (+6) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE (Cartel Spotter taken out)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Morwen doesn't so much strike the spotter as unmake his nerve — the binding-rite surges through her like the toll of that struck bell at the ford, and something in the rain-slick air answers her. The scavenger's knees buckle mid-word, his hood falling back to show a face gone slack with terror of something none of the rest of you can see, and he drops face-first into the mud between the sunken cart's ribs, out cold before he hits it. For one suspended breath the whistles in the reeds go silent — the watchers along the wreck line have just watched their spotter fall to a woman they meant to take alive, and that changes the math. Ysolde's open hands and steady voice, Aldous's blade-ready stillness, Mire's planted feet between Morwen and the reeds — none of it was needed in the end, but all of it told the hidden Cartel men exactly what price the rest would cost. The whistles fade back into the rain rather than close the trap. The party holds the dry path off Gullet Ford, Morwen unbled and unclaimed, though the Cartel will remember whose spotter came home broken — and whose vow made an enemy of men who deal in debts, not forgiveness.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The scavenger kneels in the mud where Morwen's rite dropped him, hood back, rain running down a face still slack with whatever terror she pulled loose. He's shaking too hard to run, but his eyes keep cutting past all of you, toward the broken roofline rising beyond the wreck — the dry ground you were making for. Behind that silence is the sense that he was watching that ruin, not just the ford, and that he wasn't alone out here. The rest of the party catches up as Morwen holds him with her gaze, and the question becomes whether you can get him talking before whatever he was hiding from finds you first.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: That ruin you were watching — what is it? What's coming for us?

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde steps through the rain to the Scavenger's side and crouches in the mud at his level. She waits until his eyes find hers, her presence calm but urgent — the presence of someone used to drawing truths from the desperate and the hunted.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: I've been marked by what haunts this marsh—I know that drowning fear when I see it. Whatever's in those ruins will find us faster in silence than in truth. Tell me what you saw.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous moves to the scavenger with quiet purpose, kneeling to meet his rain-slicked eyes. His weathered hands are open and steady—the hands of someone who has guided frightened people through worse. He reads the shape of the terror in the man's breathing, the clench of his shoulders, the way his gaze keeps cutting back toward those distant ruins. Aldous understands: this fear has edges, a source, a name.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: You were watching that ruin, not the ford. Whatever was waiting in there—tell me what it is. Now. I didn't break your mind just to stumble blind into it.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen closes in, not giving the scavenger room to hide. The echo of her binding-rite still shudders in the air between them—she doesn't let him forget what just happened. When she speaks, it's the voice of someone accustomed to being obeyed, each word deliberate as a hammer blow.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Look at me, not the ruins. What were you watching for out here—what's in there waiting?

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire strides between the scavenger and the broken roofline, planting herself solid in a guard stance. She's got the hard, uncompromising bearing of militia command—hand resting on her weapon, eyes sharp and steady. She holds the line, cutting his view of whatever waits in those ruins and forcing his attention back to the present threat.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — overcome with Empathy: dice - 0 + 0 → Great (+4) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — overcome with Empathy: dice + 0 - + → Great (+4) vs Mediocre (+0): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — overcome with Will: dice 0 - 0 + → Great (+4) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Three ways of asking, and the scavenger breaks on all three at once. He doesn't so much answer Ysolde's quiet question as flinch into it — words tumbling out before Aldous even finishes reading his shoulders, before Morwen's hammer-blow voice can land a second time. "Not hive-touched," he gasps, staring past them all at the broken roofline. "Worse than that. The Order sealed that place after the first outbreak — Saint Orrin's old waystation, not the temple, just a chapel-house — and something's still *in* there, singing back at the belltower across the water. Cartel sent me to see if the cellars underneath were clear for running goods through. They weren't. I saw lights moving where there's no one left to hold a lantern, and I heard the swarm-song answer from inside the walls like it was talking to something." His voice cracks. "I've been out here four days too scared to cross back through the ford alone." He gives up a name, too — Old Brannic, the Cartel factor who sent him, and the cellar route he was scouting, muttered in a rush like it might buy him mercy. Whatever the ruin is, it isn't empty, and it isn't just hive-touched — it's answering the belltower's call from a mile away, and now the party knows exactly where to look.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Ysolde and Emhain were both students of Old Tamsin, learning to read the Order's sealed ciphers in hidden places. When the Order came for Tamsin's sanctum and she fell, Emhain helped Ysolde escape with the scroll case into the reeds. They swore that night they would survive, keep studying, and read every secret the Order tried to bury. Seeing the case now, Emhain knows she lived, and he trusts her absolutely.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: I've got it—the rain's already bleeding the words away, but every cipher Tamsin drilled into me is still here. Hold it steady, Emhain. We're going to read what they died trying to hide.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde accepts the compel on 'Old Tamsin's Scroll Case'.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The barge went down under Verrick's colors—he sent us scouting the northern channels during the first great flood, wanted the Wardens' reach to expand farther than anyone had gone. I read the rain and told him no, but he ordered us out anyway. Seventeen good people drowned, and I was the only one who surfaced. I heard them calling me back down into the grey—all of them at once. That night I understood what the water was saying: I'd been marked, spared to ferry souls safely after that. I couldn't serve Verrick's colors anymore, so I walked into the reeds. But why does it terrify me more than the flood? Because Verrick won't accept that answer. He'll want to know why I lived, why I didn't save them, whether I owe him loyalty or blood-price. And I know him well enough to fear what he'll decide I owe—whether it's death or the debt of coming back into formation. Either way, my choice to walk away will have cost him something, and Verrick always collects.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: Verrick. The waters are rising behind us, and these people need to cross. I'm asking you to let them through—whatever you need from me, it can wait until they're safe on higher ground.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous accepts the compel on 'Captain Verrick's Old Discipline'.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Beat: Brother Emhain, a fellow acolyte trained under the same dead scholar as Ysolde — Old Tamsin herself — stumbles out from behind the temple's broken colonnade, soaked and half-starving, and goes still with recognition the instant he sees the scroll case at Ysolde's hip. begs the party to go to the Warden garrison at Verrick's old drill-yard — the very outpost where Aldous once served under old militia discipline, now a half-drowned stockade flying the Wardens' colors., because her son followed the swarm-song into the belltower.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Brother Emhain won't let go of the scroll case even after Ysolde takes his hand — he's shaking too hard, words spilling out in a rush about his sister's boy, gone three days now, who followed the swarm-song out past the reed line toward the belltower. The only dry route there cuts straight through Verrick's old drill-yard, a half-drowned stockade still flying Warden colors, still manned. Aldous knows every stone of that yard — knows the drill signals, knows exactly how Verrick will look at him walking back in after seventeen dead and one survivor who never answered for it. The rain hasn't slackened; somewhere behind you the ford is already closing. Emhain grips Ysolde's wrist like she's the only solid thing left in the world and says the boy's name is Fen — that he taught Fen to read a little, same as Tamsin taught them.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: I remember Fen—Tamsin taught him well. We'll find him, I swear it. But the water's rising, and we need to move.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde grips Emhain's wrist back with steady pressure, meeting his desperation with absolute certainty. Her eyes trace the dark water behind them, reading the channels like she reads the current itself—she knows exactly how long they have. She straightens, voice calm but commanding as she looks to the crew. "Aldous leads. Emhain stays with me. We're going through the yard now, before Gullet Ford closes on us.")

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: I know that yard—every signal, every stone. I'll get you through, and we'll bring Fen back. Whatever Verrick wants from me, it can wait until he's safe.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous steps forward through the rain, his posture straightening into the old militia stance he hasn't worn since the barge went down. He turns toward Emhain and the group, and despite the cold dread coiling in his chest, he points down the route toward the drill-yard—the back way through the old stables, the stores where a Warden watch won't expect them to enter. He reads the urgency in the water's rising surge and in Fen's name spoken with such desperation.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: The boy's still choosing. We go. But I want to know everything—what's at that garrison, what you haven't told us, and what those Wardens will do when we come calling.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen's hand grips the wards at her hip, her eyes fixed on Emhain with the intensity that shattered the scavenger's nerve—not cruelty, but absolute certainty. She's already turning toward the garrison, already committed, already moving forward into the rain.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: That's Verrick's old yard. I know every stone of it, every gate and guardpost. Aldous calling out to him like that will force a reckoning we don't have time for. Give me a few moments to scout the perimeter—there might be a path the rising water hasn't swallowed yet, one that doesn't put him in Verrick's reach.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire steps forward, reading the tension between Aldous and the half-drowned stockade flying Warden colors. Her jaw tightens—she recognizes the trap here, the way desperation and old debts are about to collide. She's already moving toward the reeds, her eyes tracking possible routes around the garrison, shoulders settling into the posture of someone who still knows how to hold a line, even when cast out and disgraced.)

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Mire slips into the reeds and comes back low, breathing hard but grinning through the rain. "There's a line," she says, "old pilings past the west wall — dry enough if you don't hesitate, and it comes out behind the stores, not the gate." She traces it in the mud: past Verrick's watchtower, through the drowned stable yard, up onto the drill-yard's old grain platform, and out the far side toward the belltower road — never once crossing the sightline of the main gate. It buys them the crossing without Aldous walking up and announcing himself to his old captain. But as the four of them start picking their way along the pilings, Emhain stumbling at Ysolde's side with the scroll case clutched to his chest, a bell begins to toll somewhere inside the stockade — not the swarm-song, but a Warden's watch-bell, three short strikes. Someone on that wall has eyes on the water, and the rain hasn't hidden them as well as Mire hoped.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: That's a watch-bell, not the swarm-song—they've spotted the water, not us. The flood's rising fast enough to cover our tracks if we move now. Come on.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde's eyes snap to the garrison wall, reading the pattern of the tolling bell—Wardens marking the flood's height, not signaling pursuit. She turns to the water's flow immediately, tracing how the rising current is already beginning to obscure the pilings from the watchpost's sightline. She steadies Emhain with one hand and gestures the others deeper into the drowned yard, moving lower and faster along the posts where the garrison can't follow on horseback.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: That's the watch-bell, not alarm—we have minutes before they form up at the gate. Keep moving, stay low.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous stiffens as the three-strike pattern echoes across the drill-yard, and in that moment every fiber of his old training springs alive. He reads the signal like he reads the rain: watch-bell, not alarm—a calling-in of the sighting, not a full muster. The Wardens won't move to position at the gate for several heartbeats yet. He turns sharply toward the group, one hand gesturing them forward with the low urgent clarity of someone who's stood in that drill-yard long enough to know exactly how its machinery moves.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: It's Morwen. I'm through this yard and up that belltower with or without Verrick's blessing. You can explain to him why you fought me.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps forward from the pilings and lets herself be seen fully—the exorcist of Hollowmoot, wards at her hip, ancient authority settling into her shoulders like a weight they've learned to carry. She's not hiding. The bell-ringer on that wall will recognize her, and every Warden trained under Verrick knows what it means when she appears in the rain.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: I'm right here, Verrick's watch—and I'm not running this time!

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire steps into clear sight of the watchtower, shoulders back in the militia stance she still wears despite her disgrace. She's making herself the known enemy they'll want to stop, pulling every eye on that wall toward her and away from the quiet group moving through the pilings. She's the line they'll hold their attention on now.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — create advantage with Notice: dice + + - -, invoking Reads river currents like kin [YS-01] → Great (+4) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — create advantage with Notice: dice - + - -, invoking Knows the Wardens' drill signals [AL-02] → Great (+4) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen — create advantage with Will: dice + 0 - 0 → Great (+4) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — create advantage with Provoke: dice 0 0 - -, invoking Marked enemy of the Wardens [MI-04] → Fair (+2) vs Average (+1): SUCCESS

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The bell's three strikes hang in the rain, and for one held breath the whole yard seems to turn toward the noise — toward Morwen standing in plain sight with her wards catching what little light there is, toward Mire squared up and shouting Verrick's own watch back at itself. It works better than any of them could have planned: whatever eyes were on that wall are locked on the two women who chose to be seen, while Ysolde reads the flood's own rise pulling a curtain of churned water across the pilings, and Aldous threads the group through the drill-yard's blind seconds like he never left the old formation. Emhain stumbles half-blind at Ysolde's side, scroll case clutched to his chest, and somehow none of you so much as splash loud enough to matter. By the time the watch-bell falls silent and a second pattern starts up — searching now, not spotting — you're already past the grain platform, already through the drowned stable yard, already out the far side with the belltower road opening grey and empty ahead of you. Verrick's stockade shrinks into the rain behind you, its gate never so much as opening. Emhain sobs out something that might be thanks, might be Fen's name, and points north up the road toward the flooded temple and its ringing swarm-song.

costs.text: As Morwen scans the rising ground, the broken roofline resolves into something Mire recognizes with a lurch: the shape of an old Order waystation, the kind her orphanage used to garrison her in as a child. She never had a family of blood — the Order was the only kin she ever knew — and that hollow a

costs.text: A gaunt scavenger who has been squatting inside the sunken cart wreck at Gullet Ford — watching every crossing for weeks — steps out into the rain. He's no drifter; he's a Cartel spotter, and he's been waiting for you specifically.

Word travels fast on the water: Morwen's open vow against the Wardens' torches has reached Cartel ears, and they've decided a healer who defies the men who burn houses is worth owning rather than losing to the Order or the Wardens.

The spotter names a stilt-house full of hive-touched family the Wardens will burn tonight — Morwen knows the pull of that vow, that she'll risk everything for one house, and he's counting on it. Come alone, now, to 'negotiate' with the Cartel on their terms, he says, or the family burns — and it mea

the Warden garrison at Verrick's old drill-yard — the very outpost where Aldous once served under old militia discipline, now a half-drowned stockade flying the Wardens' colors.

Emhain thrusts a waterlogged Order ledger into Ysolde's hands, begging her to read the evacuation cipher before the downpour finishes what it's already started — the ink runs in hard rain, and the garrison's real danger is bleeding into illegible streaks even as she watches.

The moment Aldous is recognized at the gate, word runs ahead of him — Verrick himself comes to the palisade to see his old man with his own eyes, and whatever welcome the party gets now depends on a debt or a grudge only Aldous remembers.

ambiguities.issue: The rule grants a Bypassed segment to any THREAT/FACTION that was 'face-up this session, faced no roll, and was not taken out,' but does not say whether a card must still be face-up at session end to qualify. T-01 (a THREAT anchor) was face-up scenes 1-3, took no roll against it, was never taken out, but was discarded from the rail at scene 3 cleanup for exceeding the 5-card limit (event 54). No Bypassed segment for T-01 appears in the post-session GM step A entries (events 120-123 only cover F-01–F-04).
ambiguities.interim_ruling: The table treated only cards still face-up at session end as eligible for the Bypassed check; T-01 was left out of the post-session accounting since it had already left the rail mid-session.

ambiguities.issue: 'Taken out in a conflict' is ambiguous as to whether the target counts as 'left alive' (mutate) or 'destroyed/fully resolved' (retire) for the post-session threat-evaluation step, since Fate's 'taken out' can mean death, capture, or incapacitation. T-03 was taken out in conflict (events 63-64) and then mutated to T-03v2 rather than retired (event 124).
ambiguities.interim_ruling: The table defaulted 'taken out in conflict' to 'left alive' (mutate with a new tag reflecting what happened, e.g. 'Broken by Morwen's Binding-Rite') unless the fiction explicitly stated the target was killed or the threat fully resolved.

friction.text: GM attempted to re-fire module M-1's trigger in scene 5 after it had already deployed in scene 3; the engine correctly refused it as 'not an unused fictional trigger' (§7), but the attempt suggests the table needed clearer guidance that a deployed module/trigger is one-shot for the session.

Three of the six deck-draw costs/compels in this session (MI-01 major cost, MO-03 surfacing compel, YS-02 surfacing compel) were initially written without clearly using the drawn card's tag and had to be repaired per the §3 'the GM rewrites it' rule — a recurring friction point suggesting the table would benefit from a tag-quoting template for compel narration.

Rail management correctly evicted the oldest non-GLOBAL GM card (T-01) when the 5-card limit was hit (event 54), but this GM anchor card then went completely unaccounted for in post-session bookkeeping (no Bypassed check, no retire/mutate entry), which could let a THREAT quietly fall out of the Chronicle.

free_text.best_moment: When Emhain appeared holding the scroll case—my backstory wasn't backstory anymore, it was urgent present action, and the GM had clearly known exactly where to place it.
free_text.most_frustrating: Negotiating with the Cartel spotter using my actual contacts and political angle, then watching Morwen just unmake him with a Will attack—felt like my approach to the problem didn't matter compared to direct power.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: My cook aspect never showed up—the crew secrets I hear, that intimate knowledge of how people break under pressure in tight spaces. Also would've pushed harder on mechanics instead of relying on good roleplay advice.
free_text.one_sentence: Backstory integrated beautifully, especially through Emhain, but I should've fought the mechanics harder instead of playing it safe with my fate points.

free_text.best_moment: Stepping between Morwen and the Cartel spotter with the iron charms and the ferryman's vow — it felt like the purest version of how Aldous plays: protecting someone else's safety ahead of his own skin, grounded in something real (the drowned people, the mark they left on him). The GM gave me a moment that *felt* earned and specific to him.
free_text.most_frustrating: The water-panic weakness was set as flavor rather than friction. Aldous is terrified of deep water, but the rising flood and the ford stayed abstract — I wanted a moment where keeping people safe forced him to actually *choose* between his fear and his vow, something that cost him mechanically or narratively. Also, Verrick got deferred rather than confronted. That setup was perfect, and then Morwen and Mire's choices meant Aldous never had to actually face him or work through that debt.
free_text.background_used: Good. The GM wove in the drowned barge, the seventeen dead, Verrick, the ferryman's vow, the militia discipline, the rain-reading — all of it naturally and in ways that made Aldous tactically valuable (the drill signals at the yard, the flood-reading at the ford). The two compels felt earned, not arbitrary.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: Face Verrick directly instead of having Morwen and Mire draw his attention. Have the water-fear create a real choice moment where protecting someone meant overcoming panic. Maybe one scene where Aldous had to navigate what he owes versus what he actually wants to do, rather than just accepting it all as inevitable.
free_text.one_sentence: Aldous's backstory was woven through the session naturally — his past made him valuable, his weaknesses got invoked meaningfully, and the story never let him off easy for the choices he'd made before.

free_text.best_moment: Dropping the Cartel spotter with my binding-rite in S3. The moment where her spiritual authority cracked through the rain and he collapsed—that was peak Morwen. The GM let me be exactly what she's supposed to be: fearless, powerful, a woman whose vow is a weapon. It was also mechanically excellent (Fantastic +6 vs Average +1) and the follow-up where the hidden men retreated rather than close the trap showed the weight of that action landing in the world.
free_text.most_frustrating: Getting to the belltower without ever actually engaging what's waiting there. Morwen is an exorcist with Lore 3 and knowledge of rites older than the Order—I wanted to prepare, investigate, maybe perform some kind of counter-ritual or warding before walking into whatever's singing back at the swarm-song. Instead she just powdered through confrontations without any real chance to use her actual expertise. The bell tower looms ahead and I don't know what's waiting.
free_text.background_used: Yes, and it landed well. The compel on my vow against the burning in S3 pulled directly from a specific moment the GM asked me to establish—the dead girl, the Wardens' torches, her aunt's fate. It created immediate, personal stakes and made Morwen an active target rather than just another member of the party. It was dramatic and felt fair. The Cartel targeting her *because* of that public vow made logical sense in the world.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: Engage with my core concept: I'm an exorcist who isn't sure the hive has souls. That's my entire philosophical framework, and it never came up except as mechanical power in my binding-rites. I wanted to actually wrestle with that question—do these creatures deserve mercy or breaking? When I spoke the rites, what was I actually doing to them? That crisis is who Morwen *is*, but the session treated her as pure power and certainty instead.
free_text.one_sentence: My vow against burning was used brilliantly for immediate dramatic stakes, but my core philosophical crisis about whether the hive-touched have souls never surfaced despite being my entire concept.

free_text.best_moment: The perimeter scout before the garrison—reading the old drill-yard I trained in, threading a route that avoided Verrick's direct attention, then choosing to step into his line of sight anyway to draw fire from the others. That mix of tactical planning and dramatic choice felt very Mire.
free_text.most_frustrating: The scavenger encounter got shut down too quickly by Morwen's Will attack before I could escalate the confrontation I'd positioned Mire for, and I wanted deeper exploration of what the Cartel debt actually means mechanically—how does her intervention affect that relationship?
free_text.background_used: Very well. The Temple orphanage triggered naturally at the ford, Verrick's drill-yard and my militia knowledge became the emotional core of the garrison scene, and the Cartel debt was immediately relevant when the spotter appeared. None of it felt forced—the GM wove these threads through without explicitly asking backstory questions.
free_text.wanted_but_couldnt: More extended confrontation with Verrick beyond catching his attention, and deeper mechanics on the Cartel side—what does Mire owe exactly, and how does sheltering Morwen from a Cartel spotter complicate that further?
free_text.one_sentence: My backstory felt threaded through as genuine complications rather than window dressing, and each past choice meant something in the present moment.

chronicle.summary: The party crossed into Verrick's half-drowned drill-yard to save Brother Emhain's nephew Fen, splitting attention as Morwen and Mire openly defied the Wardens' watch-bell while Ysolde and Aldous slipped the others through blind seconds in the flood. They escaped clean, no gate ever opening, and now stand on the belltower road with the swarm-song calling ahead. Earlier this session, the Cartel spotter Ysolde and Morwen broke in Scene 3 was left a ruined, terrified husk rather than killed outright.
